sanskrit: anyonyasya hayān viddhvā dhvajau ca sumahābalau ratheṣāṃ rathacakre ca cikrīḍatur ariṃdamau
english: Piercing each other's horses and both their banners, the two mighty subduers of foes, those great-strengthed warriors, sported also with each other's chariot-poles and chariot-wheels.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja bhīṣmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ vāsudevaṃ tribhir bāṇair ājaghāna stanāntare
english: Then, O great king, the wrathful Bhīṣma, foremost of those who strike, smote Vāsudeva with three arrows in the breast.

sanskrit: bhīṣmacāpacyutair bāṇair nirviddho madhusūdanaḥ virarāja raṇe rājan sapuṣpa iva kiṃśukaḥ
english: Pierced by the shafts loosed from Bhīṣma's bow, the slayer of Madhu shone in the battle, O king, like a kiṃśuka tree in full flower.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno bhṛśaṃ kruddho nirviddhaṃ prekṣya mādhavam gāṅgeyasārathiṃ saṃkhye nirbibheda tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Arjuna, exceedingly enraged at seeing Mādhava wounded, pierced Gāṅgeya's charioteer in the encounter with three arrows.

sanskrit: yatamānau tu tau vīrāv anyonyasya vadhaṃ prati nāśaknutāṃ tadānyonyam abhisaṃdhātum āhave
english: Though both those heroes strove for each other's destruction, they could not, in that battle, gain any opening upon one another.

sanskrit: maṇḍalāni vicitrāṇi gatapratyāgatāni ca adarśayetāṃ bahudhā sūtasāmarthyalāghavāt
english: Through the skill and deftness of their charioteers they displayed in manifold ways their wondrous wheeling courses, advancing and retreating again.

sanskrit: antaraṃ ca prahāreṣu tarkayantau mahārathau rājann antaramārgasthau sthitāv āstāṃ muhur muhuḥ
english: Watching for an opening to strike, those two great car-warriors, O king, kept their stations again and again upon the intervening paths.

sanskrit: ubhau siṃharavonmiśraṃ śaṅkhaśabdaṃ pracakratuḥ tathaiva cāpanirghoṣaṃ cakratus tau mahārathau
english: Both of them raised the blast of their conches mingled with lion-roars, and likewise those two great car-warriors made the twang of their bows resound.

sanskrit: tayoḥ śaṅkhapraṇādena rathanemisvanena ca dāritā sahasā bhūmiś cakampa ca nanāda ca
english: By the blast of their conches and the din of their chariot-wheels the earth was suddenly rent, and it quaked and roared.

sanskrit: na tayor antaraṃ kaś cid dadṛśe bharatarṣabha balinau samare śūrāv anyonyasadṛśāv ubhau
english: None, O bull of the Bhāratas, could perceive any opening in either of them; both were mighty and brave in battle, and equal to one another.

sanskrit: cihnamātreṇa bhīṣmaṃ tu prajajñus tatra kauravāḥ tathā pāṇḍusutāḥ pārthaṃ cihnamātreṇa jajñire
english: By his ensign alone could the Kauravas there recognize Bhīṣma, and likewise the sons of Pāṇḍu knew Pārtha by his ensign alone.

sanskrit: tayor nṛvarayo rājan dṛśya tādṛk parākramam vismayaṃ sarvabhūtāni jagmur bhārata saṃyuge
english: Beholding such prowess in those two best of men, O king, all beings were struck with wonder in that battle, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na tayor vivaraṃ kaś cid raṇe paśyati bhārata dharme sthitasya hi yathā na kaś cid vṛjinaṃ kva cit
english: None could see a weak point in either of them in the fight, O Bhārata, even as in a man steadfast in righteousness none can find any fault anywhere.

sanskrit: ubhau hi śarajālena tāv adṛśyau babhūvatuḥ prakāśau ca punas tūrṇaṃ babhūvatur ubhau raṇe
english: Both of them became invisible behind their net of arrows, and both again quickly became visible in the battle.

sanskrit: tatra devāḥ sagandharvāś cāraṇāś ca saharṣibhiḥ anyonyaṃ pratyabhāṣanta tayor dṛṣṭvā parākramam
english: There the gods together with the Gandharvas and the Cāraṇas, along with the seers, spoke to one another, beholding the prowess of those two.

sanskrit: na śakyau yudhi saṃrabdhau jetum etau mahārathau sadevāsuragandharvair lokair api kathaṃ cana
english: These two great car-warriors, when roused in battle, cannot be vanquished in any wise, not even by all the worlds together with their gods, Asuras, and Gandharvas.

sanskrit: āścaryabhūtaṃ lokeṣu yuddham etan mahādbhutam naitādṛśāni yuddhāni bhaviṣyanti kathaṃ cana
english: This battle, a marvel in the worlds, is exceedingly wondrous; battles such as this shall never come to pass in any way again.

sanskrit: nāpi śakyo raṇe jetuṃ bhīṣmaḥ pārthena dhīmatā sadhanuś ca rathasthaś ca pravapan sāyakān raṇe
english: Nor can Bhīṣma be conquered in the fight by the wise Pārtha, while bow in hand and stationed on his car he showers his shafts in battle.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavaṃ yuddhe devair api durāsadam na vijetuṃ raṇe bhīṣma utsaheta dhanurdharam
english: And likewise the son of Pāṇḍu, that bowman hard to assail even by the gods in battle, Bhīṣma cannot venture to vanquish in the fray.

sanskrit: iti sma vācaḥ śrūyante proccarantyas tatas tataḥ gāṅgeyārjunayoḥ saṃkhye stavayuktā viśāṃ pate
english: Such words, laden with praise of Gāṅgeya and Arjuna in their combat, were heard rising up here and there, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: tvadīyās tu tato yodhāḥ pāṇḍaveyāś ca bhārata anyonyaṃ samare jaghnus tayos tatra parākrame
english: Then thy warriors and those of the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata, smote one another in the battle amid the prowess of those two.

sanskrit: śitadhārais tathā khaḍgair vimalaiś ca paraśvadhaiḥ śarair anyaiś ca bahubhiḥ śastrair nānāvidhair yudhi ubhayoḥ senayor vīrā nyakṛntanta parasparam
english: With keen-edged swords and bright battle-axes, with arrows and with many other weapons of various kinds, the heroes of both armies cut one another down in the fight.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā ghore tasmin yuddhe sudāruṇe droṇapāñcālyayo rājan mahān āsīt samāgamaḥ
english: While that dreadful and most cruel battle was thus raging, O king, there came about a great encounter between Droṇa and the Pāñcāla prince.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kathaṃ droṇo maheṣvāsaḥ pāñcālyaś cāpi pārṣataḥ raṇe samīyatur yattau tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How did the great bowman Droṇa and the Pāñcāla son of Pṛṣata, both intent, come together in battle? Recount that to me, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: diṣṭam eva paraṃ manye pauruṣād api saṃjaya yatra śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo nātarad yudhi pāṇḍavam
english: I deem destiny supreme, even above manly effort, Saṃjaya, since Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu could not overcome the son of Pāṇḍu in the fight.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo hi samare kruddho hanyāl lokāṃś carācarān sa kathaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ yuddhe nātarat saṃjayaujasā
english: For Bhīṣma, enraged in battle, could slay the worlds with all that moves and moves not; how then could he not, by his own might, overcome the son of Pāṇḍu in the fight, Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājan sthiro bhūtvā yuddham etat sudāruṇam na śakyaḥ pāṇḍavo jetuṃ devair api savāsavaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear, O king, with a steady mind, of this most dreadful battle. The son of Pāṇḍu cannot be vanquished even by the gods led by Vāsava.

sanskrit: droṇas tu niśitair bāṇair dhṛṣṭadyumnam ayodhayat sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena rathanīḍād apātayat
english: Droṇa fought against Dhṛṣṭadyumna with sharp arrows, and with a broad-headed shaft struck down his charioteer from the chariot-box.

sanskrit: tasyātha caturo vāhāṃś caturbhiḥ sāyakottamaiḥ pīḍayām āsa saṃkruddho dhṛṣṭadyumnasya māriṣa
english: Then in his wrath, O venerable one, he afflicted the four steeds of Dhṛṣṭadyumna with four excellent shafts.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tato droṇaṃ navatyā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha prahasan vīras tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Thereupon the hero Dhṛṣṭadyumna, laughing, pierced Droṇa with ninety sharp arrows, and cried out, 'Stand! Stand!'

sanskrit: tataḥ punar ameyātmā bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān śaraiḥ pracchādayām āsa dhṛṣṭadyumnam amarṣaṇam
english: Then once more the immeasurable and valorous son of Bhāradvāja covered with his shafts the wrathful Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: ādade ca śaraṃ ghoraṃ pārṣatasya vadhaṃ prati śakrāśanisamasparśaṃ mṛtyudaṇḍam ivāparam
english: And he took up a dreadful arrow for the slaying of Pṛṣata's son, of touch like Śakra's thunderbolt, like a second rod of Death.

sanskrit: hāhākāro mahān āsīt sarvasainyasya bhārata tam iṣuṃ saṃdhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhāradvājena saṃyuge
english: A great cry of dismay arose from all the host, O Bhārata, when they saw that shaft fitted to the string by the son of Bhāradvāja in the encounter.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma dhṛṣṭadyumnasya pauruṣam yad ekaḥ samare vīras tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: Therein we beheld a wondrous feat of manliness in Dhṛṣṭadyumna, that the hero alone in battle stood firm as an unmoving mountain.

sanskrit: taṃ ca dīptaṃ śaraṃ ghoram āyāntaṃ mṛtyum ātmanaḥ ciccheda śaravṛṣṭiṃ ca bhāradvāje mumoca ha
english: And that blazing, dreadful arrow speeding toward him, his own death, he cut asunder, and let loose a shower of arrows upon the son of Bhāradvāja.

sanskrit: tata uccukruśuḥ sarve pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha dhṛṣṭadyumnena tat karma kṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā suduṣkaram
english: Then all the Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas raised a shout, beholding that most difficult feat accomplished by Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaktiṃ mahāvegāṃ svarṇavaiḍūryabhūṣitām droṇasya nidhanākāṅkṣī cikṣepa sa parākramī
english: Then that valiant one, longing for Droṇa's death, hurled a swift lance adorned with gold and lapis.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā śaktiṃ kanakabhūṣaṇām tridhā cikṣepa samare bhāradvājo hasann iva
english: That gold-decked lance rushing suddenly upon him, the son of Bhāradvāja, as if laughing, cut into three pieces in the battle.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ vinihatāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ pratāpavān vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi droṇaṃ prati janeśvara
english: Seeing his lance struck down, the valorous Dhṛṣṭadyumna poured showers of arrows upon Droṇa, O lord of men.

sanskrit: śaravarṣaṃ tatas taṃ tu saṃnivārya mahāyaśāḥ droṇo drupadaputrasya madhye ciccheda kārmukam
english: Then the illustrious Droṇa, warding off that shower of arrows, cut asunder in the middle the bow of Drupada's son.

sanskrit: sa cchinnadhanvā samare gadāṃ gurvīṃ mahāyaśāḥ droṇāya preṣayām āsa girisāramayīṃ balī
english: His bow being severed, that mighty and illustrious one hurled at Droṇa in the battle a heavy mace made of mountain-stuff.

sanskrit: sā gadā vegavan muktā prāyād droṇajighāṃsayā tatrādbhutam apaśyāma bhāradvājasya vikramam
english: That mace, loosed with force, sped on, eager to slay Droṇa; therein we beheld a wondrous feat of prowess in the son of Bhāradvāja.

sanskrit: lāghavād vyaṃsayām āsa gadāṃ hemavibhūṣitām vyaṃsayitvā gadāṃ tāṃ ca preṣayām āsa pārṣate
english: By his deftness he turned aside that gold-adorned mace, and having turned it aside, he sent forth arrows upon Pṛṣata's son.

sanskrit: bhallān suniśitān pītān svarṇapuṅkhāñ śilāśitān te tasya kavacaṃ bhittvā papuḥ śoṇitam āhave
english: Well-sharpened broad-headed shafts, dyed yellow, gold-feathered, and whetted on stone — they pierced his armor and drank his blood in the fight.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya dhṛṣṭadyumno mahāmanāḥ droṇaṃ yudhi parākramya śarair vivyādha pañcabhiḥ
english: Then the high-souled Dhṛṣṭadyumna, taking up another bow and pressing forward against Droṇa in the fight, pierced him with five arrows.

sanskrit: rudhirāktau tatas tau tu śuśubhāte nararṣabhau vasantasamaye rājan puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Then those two bulls among men, smeared with blood, shone forth, O king, like two kiṃśuka trees in flower in the springtime.

sanskrit: amarṣitas tato rājan parākramya camūmukhe droṇo drupadaputrasya punaś ciccheda kārmukam
english: Then, full of indignation, O king, and pressing forward at the head of the host, Droṇa again cut asunder the bow of Drupada's son.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ avākirad ameyātmā vṛṣṭyā megha ivācalam
english: Then the immeasurable one overwhelmed him, his bow severed, with smooth-jointed arrows, as a cloud drenches a mountain with rain.

sanskrit: sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena rathanīḍād apātayat athāsya caturo vāhāṃś caturbhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And with a broad-headed shaft he struck down his charioteer from the chariot-box, and then his four steeds with four sharp arrows —

sanskrit: pātayām āsa samare siṃhanādaṃ nanāda ca tato 'pareṇa bhallena hastāc cāpam athācchinat
english: these he felled in the battle, and he uttered a lion-roar; then with another broad-headed shaft he cut the bow from his hand.

sanskrit: sa cchinnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ gadāpāṇir avārohat khyāpayan pauruṣaṃ mahat
english: His bow severed, his car gone, his steeds slain, his charioteer killed, he descended mace in hand, making known his great manhood.

sanskrit: tām asya viśikhais tūrṇaṃ pātayām āsa bhārata rathād anavarūḍhasya tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: That mace, too, Droṇa swiftly struck down with his shafts, O Bhārata, before he had even descended from the car; that seemed a wonder.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa vipulaṃ carma śatacandraṃ ca bhānumat khaḍgaṃ ca vipulaṃ divyaṃ pragṛhya subhujo balī
english: Then that strong, fair-armed hero, seizing a broad shield marked with a hundred moons and gleaming bright, and a broad celestial sword,

sanskrit: abhidudrāva vegena droṇasya vadhakāṅkṣayā āmiṣārthī yathā siṃho vane mattam iva dvipam
english: rushed forward with speed, longing to slay Droṇa, as a lion seeking prey rushes upon a rutting elephant in the forest.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma bhāradvājasya pauruṣam lāghavaṃ cāstrayogaṃ ca balaṃ bāhvoś ca bhārata
english: Therein we beheld a wondrous feat of manliness in the son of Bhāradvāja — his deftness, his mastery of weapons, and the strength of his arms, O Bhārata —

sanskrit: yad enaṃ śaravarṣeṇa vārayām āsa pārṣatam na śaśāka tato gantuṃ balavān api saṃyuge
english: in that he held off Pṛṣata's son with a shower of arrows, so that, mighty though he was, he could not advance in the battle.

sanskrit: tatra sthitam apaśyāma dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ mahāratham vārayāṇaṃ śaraughāṃś ca carmaṇā kṛtahastavat
english: There we beheld the great car-warrior Dhṛṣṭadyumna standing firm, warding off the floods of arrows with his shield, like one of practiced hand.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhuḥ sahasābhyapatad balī sāhāyyakārī samare pārṣatasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then the mighty-armed and strong Bhīma suddenly rushed up, rendering aid in the battle to the high-souled son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: sa droṇaṃ niśitair bāṇai rājan vivyādha saptabhiḥ pārṣataṃ ca tadā tūrṇam anyam āropayad ratham
english: He pierced Droṇa, O king, with seven sharp arrows, and then quickly mounted Pṛṣata's son upon another car.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā kaliṅgaṃ samacodayat sainyena mahatā yuktaṃ bhāradvājasya rakṣaṇe
english: Then King Duryodhana urged on the Kaliṅga, attended by a great host, for the protection of the son of Bhāradvāja.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā mahatī senā kaliṅgānāṃ janeśvara bhīmam abhyudyayau tūrṇaṃ tava putrasya śāsanāt
english: Then that great host of the Kaliṅgas, O lord of men, advanced swiftly upon Bhīma at thy son's command.

sanskrit: pāñcālyam abhisaṃtyajya droṇo 'pi rathināṃ varaḥ virāṭadrupadau vṛddhau yodhayām āsa saṃgatau dhṛṣṭadyumno 'pi samare dharmarājaṃ samabhyayāt
english: And Droṇa too, that foremost of car-warriors, leaving the Pāñcāla prince, gave battle to the aged Virāṭa and Drupada, who had joined together; and Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the battle went forth to the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam kaliṅgānāṃ ca samare bhīmasya ca mahātmanaḥ jagataḥ prakṣayakaraṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam
english: Then there arose a tumultuous, hair-raising battle between the Kaliṅgas and the high-souled Bhīma, world-destroying, of dreadful form, and terrifying.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tathā pratisamādiṣṭaḥ kaliṅgo vāhinīpatiḥ katham adbhutakarmāṇaṃ bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Being thus commanded, how did the Kaliṅga, that leader of hosts, fight in battle, together with his army, against the mighty Bhīmasena of wondrous deeds —

sanskrit: carantaṃ gadayā vīraṃ daṇḍapāṇim ivāntakam yodhayām āsa samare kaliṅgaḥ saha senayā
english: that hero ranging with his mace like Death himself with rod in hand? How did the Kaliṅga, with his army, give him battle in the encounter?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca putreṇa tava rājendra sa tathokto mahābalaḥ mahatyā senayā guptaḥ prāyād bhīmarathaṃ prati
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed by thy son, O king of kings, that mighty one, guarded by a great host, set forth against Bhīma's car.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā kaliṅgānāṃ mahācamūm rathanāgāśvakalilāṃ pragṛhītamahāyudhām
english: That great host of the Kaliṅgas rushing suddenly on, thick with chariots, elephants, and horses, its mighty weapons raised —

sanskrit: bhīmasenaḥ kaliṅgānām ārchad bhārata vāhinīm ketumantaṃ ca naiṣādim āyāntaṃ saha cedibhiḥ
english: Bhīmasena assailed that army of the Kaliṅgas, O Bhārata, and Ketumat the Niṣāda prince advancing with the Cedis.

sanskrit: tataḥ śrutāyuḥ saṃkruddho rājñā ketumatā saha āsasāda raṇe bhīmaṃ vyūḍhānīkeṣu cediṣu
english: Then Śrutāyus, sorely enraged, together with King Ketumat, encountered Bhīma in the battle, while the Cedi ranks were arrayed.

sanskrit: rathair anekasāhasraiḥ kaliṅgānāṃ janādhipaḥ ayutena gajānāṃ ca niṣādaiḥ saha ketumān bhīmasenaṃ raṇe rājan samantāt paryavārayat
english: With many thousands of cars, the lord of the Kaliṅgas, and Ketumat with ten thousand elephants and with the Niṣādas, beset Bhīmasena, O king, on every side in the battle.

sanskrit: cedimatsyakarūṣāś ca bhīmasenapurogamāḥ abhyavartanta sahasā niṣādān saha rājabhiḥ
english: And the Cedis, Matsyas, and Karūṣas, with Bhīmasena at their head, suddenly advanced upon the Niṣādas together with their kings.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam prajānan na ca yodhān svān parasparajighāṃsayā
english: Then there arose a battle of dreadful form and terrifying, the warriors in their lust to slay one another no longer knowing their own.

sanskrit: ghoram āsīt tato yuddhaṃ bhīmasya sahasā paraiḥ yathendrasya mahārāja mahatyā daityasenayā
english: Then dreadful was Bhīma's sudden battle with the foe, O great king, like that of Indra with the great host of the Daityas.

sanskrit: tasya sainyasya saṃgrāme yudhyamānasya bhārata babhūva sumahāñ śabdaḥ sāgarasyeva garjataḥ
english: From that army warring in the encounter, O Bhārata, there arose a mighty roar like that of the thundering sea.

sanskrit: anyonyasya tadā yodhā nikṛntanto viśāṃ pate mahīṃ cakruś citāṃ sarvāṃ śaśaśoṇitasaṃnibhām
english: The warriors then, cutting one another down, O lord of peoples, made the whole earth strewn over and red as the blood of a hare.

sanskrit: yodhāṃś ca svān parān vāpi nābhyajānañ jighāṃsayā svān apy ādadate svāś ca śūrāḥ samaradurjayāḥ
english: In their eagerness to slay, the warriors knew neither their own nor the foe; the heroes, hard to vanquish in battle, struck down even their own and their own kin.

sanskrit: vimardaḥ sumahān āsīd alpānāṃ bahubhiḥ saha kaliṅgaiḥ saha cedīnāṃ niṣādaiś ca viśāṃ pate
english: A very great slaughter there was of the few against the many — of the Cedis against the Kaliṅgas and the Niṣādas, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: kṛtvā puruṣakāraṃ tu yathāśakti mahābalāḥ bhīmasenaṃ parityajya saṃnyavartanta cedayaḥ
english: Having put forth their manly might to the utmost, the strong Cedis abandoned Bhīmasena and turned back.

sanskrit: sarvaiḥ kaliṅgair āsannaḥ saṃnivṛtteṣu cediṣu svabāhubalam āsthāya na nyavartata pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Though beset by all the Kaliṅgas when the Cedis had withdrawn, the son of Pāṇḍu, relying on the strength of his own arms, did not turn back.

sanskrit: na cacāla rathopasthād bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ śitair avākiran bāṇaiḥ kaliṅgānāṃ varūthinīm
english: The mighty Bhīmasena stirred not from his place upon the car, and overwhelmed the host of the Kaliṅgas with his keen arrows.
